close.summary: Sprint 5 certified the real legacy-debt incident through source, packaged candidate, temporary copies, Doctor, recertification, and Lens.
recommendations: Before npm publication, commit the certified 4.44.0 changes, run hosted CI, and publish only after its separate release gate passes.
After publication, update the installed Kyro runtime deliberately; do not treat the current 4.43.5 global runtime as the 4.44.0 candidate.
learnings: A local fixture-only or source-only pass is insufficient for release; the actual scope must be exercised by the isolated packaged runtime and independently verified by Lens.
A test flake must be reproduced in isolation before assigning blame to shared state; the assistant-chat issue was an in-flight disabled-control synchronization race.

beforeClose.title: Canonical Debt Contract and Legacy Remediation
beforeClose.objective: Reconcile Kyro and Lens debt input semantics and deliver a typed append-only canonicalization path that repairs and recertifies closed legacy scopes without changing immutable history.
successCriteria: Kyro and Lens classify every canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported debt fixture identically.
An operator can prepare, preview, and atomically canonicalize the motivating legacy debt without manually calculating digests or editing managed files.
A successful repair changes only the targeted live debt and appended provenance while every historical artifact and commitment remains byte-identical.
Doctor, status, recertification, and Lens independently agree that a valid corrected scope is remediated or recertified and reject every forged, stale, partial, or unsupported variant.
The faithful original-incident scenario passes through the isolated package and projected runtime before publication.

requirements.statement: Kyro and Lens must distinguish canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported raw debts using the same observable contract.
requirements.rationale: Raw compatibility and canonical output are different responsibilities. Shared golden vectors, including the original D1 variants, must prove identical classification and canonical projection so the output interface is never again mistaken for the input schema.

requirements.statement: All new debt writes and successful remediations must emit exactly the seven-field canonical debt representation.
requirements.rationale: The canonical key set is id, title, origin, priority, status, targetSprint, and note. Exact output prevents hybrid legacy shapes while compatibility readers remain able to diagnose old input.

requirements.statement: A new versioned debt canonicalization operation must bind the complete observed debt and produce an explicit exact canonical after-image.
requirements.rationale: The existing origin-only operation cannot repair the motivating scope. A closed debt.canonicalize operation must preserve identity fields, require explicit canonical values, retire legacy-only keys, use a whole-debt SHA-256 precondition, and resolve multiple field issues atomically without becoming a generic patch.

requirements.statement: Preparation and preview must be read-only, derive all technical digests, expose evidence and unresolved decisions, and never treat suggested values as operator authorization.
requirements.rationale: Origin has strong addedSprint evidence, while priority and target sprint remain business judgments. INPUT_REQUIRED must name every unresolved value, and a complete manifest must be producible without hand-editing managed state or manually calculating hashes.

requirements.statement: Canonicalization apply and resume must remain atomic, append-only, idempotent, and history-preserving under the state-writer lock.
requirements.rationale: Checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, ledger commitment, task, verdict, unrelated debt, and existing provenance bytes are immutable. Stale full-debt state, interruption, or post-write mismatch must produce no competing applied record and must preserve deterministic PREPARED resume.

requirements.statement: Doctor, status, replay, and recertification must support existing and new remediation versions without weakening historical integrity or tamper detection.
requirements.rationale: The new operation requires an explicit protocol revision so old readers fail closed as unsupported. New readers must replay v1, v2, new, and mixed chains; historical schema notes must never short-circuit artifact digest checks; C-NNN must bind the current head.

requirements.statement: Lens must independently verify and render legacy classification, canonicalization provenance, remediation state, and recertification state.
requirements.rationale: Lens is a read-only verifier, not a consumer of Kyro's claimed label. It must recompute commitments and result state, render selected values and retired legacy keys, and show actionable diagnostics with no stale-state fallback.

requirements.statement: A faithful original-incident fixture and a temporary-copy probe of the actual local scope must gate the packaged and installed release.
requirements.rationale: Synthetic canonical fixtures missed the contradiction. Sentinel assertions must preserve the string origin and missing-field shapes; the full before, prepare, preview, apply, Doctor, recertify, and Lens flow must pass with unchanged historical hashes through an isolated package and projected runtime.

requirements.statement: Release documentation must state the Kyro 4.43.5 limitation, compatible upgrade order, operator workflow, and exact certification boundary.
requirements.rationale: Users must not be told that origin-only remediation repairs record-level legacy drift. Documentation must separate local/source success from package, installed-runtime, Lens, and publication evidence.

nonGoals: Rewrite or replace historical checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, or ledger evidence.
Introduce generic JSON Patch or arbitrary path mutation.
Infer priority, target sprint, origin, or note semantics without explicit operator authorization.
Recover missing or corrupted checkpoint bytes from backup or Git.
Canonicalize tasks, verdicts, ADRs, conventions, or non-debt SprintFile structures.
Mutate every legacy scope automatically during installation or Doctor.
Retain legacy-only debt keys in the corrected live canonical object.
Break or rewrite existing v1 or v2 remediation and certification records.
Modify, stage, or commit files in the original Aliva checkout during release validation.
Claim production readiness beyond the covered debt compatibility and append-only remediation contract.

conventions.rule: Never rewrite committed checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, or ledger commitments; remediation may only append provenance and replace the live canonical projection.
Treat inferred legacy values as suggestions only; apply requires explicit operator-supplied canonical values in the manifest.
Every raw-debt classification or canonical projection change must update and pass the shared Kyro and Lens golden vectors.
Do not claim the incident fixed until the faithful legacy fixture passes source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens gates.
Probe the actual Aliva scope only through read-only inspection and a temporary copy; never mutate, stage, or commit its checkout during Kyro release validation.

adrs.title: Separate raw debt compatibility from canonical debt output
adrs.context: The incident recurred because Kyro treated the strict Debt output interface as the raw input contract while Lens intentionally normalizes legacy input.
adrs.decision: Classify raw debt as canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, or unsupported, and preserve an exact seven-field canonical output contract for all new writes.
consequences: Doctor and Lens can understand legacy data without calling it canonical, and writers remain strict.
Shared behavior vectors become a compatibility contract across repositories.
alternatives: Use one strict schema for both input and output.
Allow Lens-only defaults without a Kyro classification.

adrs.title: Canonicalize legacy debt as one typed record-level operation
adrs.context: The existing debt.origin.set operation cannot add missing canonical fields or retire legacy-only keys, so strict post-state validation makes the motivating scope unrecoverable.
adrs.decision: Introduce a closed debt.canonicalize operation with a whole-debt digest precondition, preserved identity fields, explicit canonical values, and an exact seven-key after-image.
consequences: One atomic R-NNN resolves all related field issues without intermediate hybrid states.
Routine isolated edits remain owned by normal debt commands rather than remediation.
alternatives: Add independent setters for every debt field.
Expose generic JSON Patch or JSON Pointer mutations.

adrs.title: Version the canonicalization operation as a new protocol revision
adrs.context: Existing Kyro and Lens readers know only the current remediation versions and debt.origin.set semantics.
adrs.decision: Publish debt.canonicalize in a new explicit remediation protocol revision with version-aware replay and mixed-chain coverage.
consequences: Older readers fail closed as unsupported instead of interpreting a known version differently.
New readers must preserve byte-compatible verification of every existing v1 and v2 chain.
alternatives: Add the new operation silently to an existing schema version.
Drop replay support for older remediation records.

adrs.title: Require explicit semantic authority and retire live legacy keys
adrs.context: AddedSprint supports an origin suggestion, but priority and target sprint are business decisions; retaining detail, resolution, or addedSprint would leave a hybrid live contract.
adrs.decision: Preparation may suggest values with evidence, but apply requires explicit operator values and emits exactly the seven canonical debt keys while preserving old bytes only through immutable history and remediation provenance.
consequences: The record distinguishes observed evidence from operator judgment.
Legacy-only keys disappear from live state without erasing historical proof.
alternatives: Silently adopt Lens defaults as historical truth.
Keep legacy-only keys alongside canonical fields.

adrs.title: Gate release on the motivating artifact shape
adrs.context: Synthetic fixtures with otherwise canonical debt allowed the previous implementation to pass while the real model-catalog-and-routing scope remained impossible to remediate.
adrs.decision: Require a faithful minimized fixture plus a temporary-copy probe of the actual scope through source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens before publication.
consequences: Fixture sentinel assertions prevent future cleanup from deleting the failure shape.
The original Aliva checkout remains read-only throughout certification.
alternatives: Certify only generated canonical fixtures.
Apply the candidate directly to the original project checkout.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Five sprints follow the dependency chain and isolate independent failure domains. Sprint 1 freezes the raw/canonical contract and faithful reproduction before writers depend on it. Sprint 2 adds the versioned typed operation and operator preparation under the existing transaction model. Sprint 3 proves replay, Doctor, status, and recertification integrity across old, new, and mixed chains. Sprint 4 updates Lens as an independent cross-repository verifier only after Kyro's protocol stabilizes. Sprint 5 certifies the faithful original incident through packaging, projected runtime, Lens, and documentation. Fewer sprints would let writer, verifier, consumer, or release evidence falsely certify one another; more would split cohesive gates without reducing risk. The plan's acceptance matrix is allocated to the relevant sprint as Given/When/Then scenarios during per-sprint planning.

sprints.title: Debt contract reconciliation and faithful fixtures

recommendations: Keep Sprint 2 limited to the typed operation schema and read-only preparation; do not introduce apply or mutate immutable history before the transaction and replay gates in Sprint 3.
Sprint 3 must implement atomic apply, resume, replay, and recertification under the state-writer lock without weakening historical integrity.
Lens contract parity in Sprint 4 requires independent verification of the new canonicalization provenance and remediation state.
Sprint 4 must independently verify v3 canonicalization provenance, unanchored or PREPARED records, and chain-head-bound recertification in Lens.
Keep Lens read-only and mirror Kyro fail-closed chain semantics without trusting Kyro status labels.
Sprint 5 must resolve the deferred Lens assistant draft-store isolation failure under a pinned supported Node runtime before claiming a green release suite.
Sprint 5 must run the faithful original incident only in a temporary copy through source, isolated package, installed or projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens without touching Aliva.
Sprint 5 must publish R9 operator documentation with the 4.43.5 origin-only limitation, upgrade order, and exact evidence boundary.

phases.title: Stable independent verifier baseline
phases.objective: Resolve the deferred Lens test-isolation defect under a supported, explicit Node runtime before using Lens as release evidence.

tasks.title: Eliminate Lens assistant draft-store test leakage
tasks.description: Reproduce and fix debt-2 in the Lens checkout under an explicitly pinned supported Node 22 runtime. Identify the cross-file state boundary for assistant-chat composer drafts, make reset/ownership deterministic without weakening per-chat draft behavior, and add a regression that fails when another test file changes worker ordering. Do not mask the failure by serializing all tests, retrying failed tests, or clearing unrelated global state.
tasks.context: debt-2 is a real ordering-dependent test leak, distinct from the Node 25 localStorage environment artifact already resolved as debt-1. Lens remains a read-only verifier; preserve existing user-visible per-chat composer drafts and test the real store lifecycle rather than introducing cleanup that production does not have.
acceptance_criteria: The assistant-chat draft store has an explicit test-safe ownership/reset boundary, and the active-chat clearing behavior remains correct while other chats retain their drafts.
A regression test reproduces cross-file or reordered execution and fails against the leaky implementation without relying on retries or a fixed test order.
Under an explicitly reported supported Node 22 runtime, three consecutive complete Lens test runs pass with no assistant-chat failure; focused tests, typecheck, and build also pass.
The recorded evidence distinguishes the supported Node runtime from Node 25's known native-localStorage behavior and resolves debt-2 only after the full-run evidence passes.

evidence.summary: debt-2 reproduced under Node v22.22.1 and root-caused: it is neither a cross-file leak nor a draft-store defect. assistant-chat.test.tsx advanced past an in-flight send as soon as the streamed reply text rendered, while sending was still true; AssistantSessionList renders session buttons disabled={busy} (busy = sending || sessionBusy), so HTMLElement.click() on a disabled button was a silent no-op and the chat never switched. The assertion then read the sending chat's empty draft. No composerDrafts writer in assistant.tsx ever removes another session's draft.
validation: Reproduction, Node v22.22.1: full suite 877 passed / 1 failed, assistant-chat 'clears only the active chat draft after a successful send', expected '' to be 'parked-draft'.

Isolation disproves cross-file: same file alone (102 tests) failed 1 of 3 runs; single test alone passed 5 of 5. Failure is intra-file and timing-dependent, contradicting debt-2's cross-file/worker-order framing.
Mechanism confirmed by source: assistant-session-list.tsx:310 disabled={busy}; assistant.tsx:1501 busy={sending || sessionBusy}; assistant.tsx:1379 handleSelectSession early-returns when sending.

Fix: added clickWhenEnabled() test helper that waits for the control to be enabled before clicking and fails loudly if it never enables. No retries, no test-order pinning, no suite serialization, no global-state clearing, no production change.

Regression added: 'blocks chat switching until a turn settles, without touching parked drafts' gates the fake provider's stream to hold a turn open, asserts every session button is disabled in that window, asserts a click in that window is a no-op, then asserts the other chat's parked draft survives after settle.

Regression is load-bearing: mutating assistant-session-list.tsx disabled={busy} to disabled={false} makes it fail at assistant-chat.test.tsx:4677 ('session switching must be blocked in flight', expected true received false). Source restored, git diff --stat empty.
Node v22.22.1: five consecutive full runs, each 64 test files / 879 tests passed, 0 failed (three required).

CORRECTION to this task's original evidence. The typecheck first recorded here ('tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json exit 0') was VACUOUS: Lens's root tsconfig.json is a solution file with files:[] and project references, so -p on it checks nothing and exits 0 in about 0.04s. Discovered during T5.5 because the matrix step was implausibly fast. Re-verified with the real command, node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -b --force on Node v22.22.1: exit 0 in 3.0s. The typecheck claim holds; the original method did not establish it.
Node v22.22.1: vite build ok; node scripts/check-guard-mutations.mjs exit 0, 16 assertions over 4 guards.
Runtime distinction: all evidence above is Node v22.22.1 (engines >=20). Node v25.2.1 remains separately known-bad because its native localStorage shadows jsdom's; no Node 25 result is used here.
evidence.notes: debt-2's recorded diagnosis was wrong on both counts (cross-file, draft-store leak). The real defect was in the test's synchronization with the send lifecycle. No assistant.tsx or assistant-session-list.tsx change was needed or made; per-chat draft behavior is unchanged. Evidence re-recorded to correct a vacuous typecheck claim.

checked_criteria: A regression test reproduces cross-file or reordered execution and fails against the leaky implementation without relying on retries or a fixed test order.
Under an explicitly reported supported Node 22 runtime, three consecutive complete Lens test runs pass with no assistant-chat failure; focused tests, typecheck, and build also pass.
The recorded evidence distinguishes the supported Node runtime from Node 25's known native-localStorage behavior and resolves debt-2 only after the full-run evidence passes.

waived_criteria.criterion: The assistant-chat draft store has an explicit test-safe ownership/reset boundary, and the active-chat clearing behavior remains correct while other chats retain their drafts.
waived_criteria.reason: Premise disproved. The draft store is component-local React state in assistant.tsx and no writer removes another session's draft, so there is no ownership/reset boundary to add; introducing test-only reset would add cleanup production does not have. The second half is verified: the sending chat's draft clears and the other chat's parked draft survives, asserted by both the original test and the new regression.

findings.detail: The typecheck evidence originally recorded for this task was vacuous (tsc -p against a solution-style tsconfig checks nothing). Re-verified with tsc -b --force, exit 0. The aggregate matrix now fails any Lens typecheck that completes in under a second.

debt-2's recorded diagnosis (cross-file leak in the draft store) was incorrect; the real defect was the test's synchronization with the send lifecycle. Captured in the debt resolution note so the misdiagnosis is not inherited.

phases.title: Faithful incident execution matrix
phases.objective: Turn the exact observed legacy shape into a reproducible, fail-closed source/package/runtime/Lens acceptance gate without touching Aliva.

tasks.title: Build the isolated source and package incident harness
tasks.description: Add one deterministic Kyro release harness that starts from the faithful D1 raw shape and its historical checkpoint variants, inventories immutable bytes and SHA-256 values, then runs source dist and a tarball installed into a fresh temporary prefix. The harness must prove the pre-remediation refusal, read-only prepare/preview, explicit operator-authorized v3 canonicalization, atomic apply/resume semantics, Doctor, and recertification. It must label the checked-out global 4.43.5 runtime as a compatibility observation, never as evidence that the candidate package was exercised.
tasks.context: R8 requires source, isolated package, projected or temporary installed candidate runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens. The installed global 4.43.5 currently supports only debt.origin.set, so its outcome must be a truthful limitation check; never overwrite ~/.agents/kyro/current or treat it as the candidate package.
acceptance_criteria: The harness starts from the faithful D1 shape: a present string origin plus the original readable legacy keys and absent canonical values. Sentinel mutations that remove the string origin or legacy shape make the harness fail.

Before/after SHA-256 inventories prove every checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and existing ledger commitment is byte-identical; only permitted live projection and append-only remediation/certification artifacts change in the temporary fixture.

Both source dist and a tarball installed in a fresh temporary prefix execute the same complete candidate flow and reach Doctor clean plus a current chain-head-bound recertification; source and package assertions cannot share only an expected label.

The harness has no write target outside its temporary directory and refuses an unresolved, non-temporary, or original-worktree path. It reports global 4.43.5 capability/version separately and never rewrites or upgrades it.

evidence.summary: Added scripts/check-original-incident-release.mjs, wired as npm run check:original-incident-release. It proves the faithful D1 incident end to end against two runtimes independently: the built source dist, and the candidate tarball produced by npm pack and installed into a fresh temporary prefix. 354 assertions pass. It also forced a real release-integrity fix: the candidate reported the same version 4.43.5 as the shipped origin-only runtime while having debt.canonicalize, so the candidate was bumped to 4.44.0.
validation: node scripts/check-original-incident-release.mjs exit 0, 354 assertions. Report: candidate kyro-ai@4.44.0 packed+installed to a temp prefix, full flow green; source dist 4.44.0 full flow green asserted independently; canonical result origin=1 priority=high targetSprint=null, retired addedSprint/detail/resolution; global runtime 4.43.5 ORIGIN-ONLY, observation only.

Faithful shape asserted from fixtures/debt-contract/golden.json: live D1 keeps a string origin, keeps detail/resolution/addedSprint, and has neither priority nor targetSprint; historical-d1-sprint-1 and -2 keep string origins.

Sentinel proven to bite: 9 in-memory cleanups of the corpus (origin canonicalized to 1, origin deleted, each of detail/resolution/addedSprint removed, priority filled in, targetSprint filled in, the live D1 case deleted, a historical variant canonicalized) are each required to make the shape assertion throw.

Write-target safety proven, not merely claimed: assertTemporary refuses the Kyro checkout, a directory inside it, the home directory, and any unresolved relative path; every fixture root, rehearsal and probe dir is asserted to resolve under the OS temp root, and HOME is redirected into the fixture so nothing reaches the real ~/.agents.

Immutability: SHA-256 inventory of every archive checkpoint/.checkpoint.json, snapshot/.json and narrative/.md plus a digest of every existing ledger entry, compared after the read-only phase, after canonicalization, and at end of flow. Remediation and certification artifacts are excluded as the only things permitted to grow.

Flow covered per runtime: pre-remediation doctor refusal naming origin; canonicalize-prepare INPUT_REQUIRED naming origin/priority/targetSprint with no manifest and no write; prepare READY at schemaVersion 3 with one debt.canonicalize op and still no write; canonicalize-preview accepted read-only; replanted record visible as R-001 PREPARED; remediate apply resuming byte-for-byte with no duplicate R-002; exactly seven canonical keys in order with operator-authorized values; legacy keys retired; D2 untouched; recorded after-image equal to live and retiredKeys exact; doctor exit 0 reporting 'replayed through R-001'; status remediated; recertify apply bound to the chain head read from the immutable C-001 record; status recertified; doctor clean.

Source and package do not share a label: runIncidentFlow executes the whole sequence separately per runtime and re-derives after-image, retiredKeys, chain head, record schemaVersion and reported version from that runtime's own output; equality between them is asserted only afterwards.

Package completeness asserted from the installed tree: dist/cli.js, fixtures/debt-contract/golden.json, scripts/check-original-incident-release.mjs, config.json and WORKFLOW.yaml all present, and the packaged golden corpus is digest-equal to the source corpus and passes the same faithful-shape sentinel.
Global runtime handled as observation only: probed for --version and remediate --help in a temp cwd, never written, never used as candidate evidence; presence re-asserted unchanged after the probe.
npm run build exit 0; node scripts/check-versions.mjs reports All versions match: 4.44.0.
evidence.notes: Version bump 4.43.5 -> 4.44.0 across package.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, WORKFLOW.yaml and package-lock.json per CLAUDE.md. Reason: the gate must tell the candidate apart from the shipped origin-only runtime, and T5.4 must document 'X adds debt.canonicalize' without contradicting '4.43.5 is origin-only'. The gate now fails if an origin-only runtime ever shares the candidate's version string. This is a working-tree change only: nothing committed, nothing published, ~/.agents/kyro/current untouched. T5.3's --original-scope probe is implemented in the same file but reports not-requested until T5.3 runs it.

checked_criteria: The harness starts from the faithful D1 shape: a present string origin plus the original readable legacy keys and absent canonical values. Sentinel mutations that remove the string origin or legacy shape make the harness fail.

Before/after SHA-256 inventories prove every checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and existing ledger commitment is byte-identical; only permitted live projection and append-only remediation/certification artifacts change in the temporary fixture.

Both source dist and a tarball installed in a fresh temporary prefix execute the same complete candidate flow and reach Doctor clean plus a current chain-head-bound recertification; source and package assertions cannot share only an expected label.

The harness has no write target outside its temporary directory and refuses an unresolved, non-temporary, or original-worktree path. It reports global 4.43.5 capability/version separately and never rewrites or upgrades it.

findings.detail: The candidate required a version bump to 4.44.0 because it shipped debt.canonicalize while still reporting 4.43.5, the version of the origin-only runtime users have installed. The gate now refuses that collision, but the bump is an uncommitted working-tree change awaiting a separately authorized release decision.

tasks.title: Probe the actual incident only through a temporary copy and Lens
tasks.description: Locate the actual local model-catalog-and-routing scope by read-only inspection, verify its observed D1 shape and immutable inventory, and copy only the verified project/scope input into a newly created temporary directory. Run the candidate package flow there, then load that temporary resulting scope through Lens's real parser, provenance resolver, and focused UI contract tests. The original checkout must remain byte-for-byte unchanged and un-staged.
tasks.context: The original scope is evidence, not a test fixture under Kyro's authority. Follow aliva-readonly-probe exactly: discovery and hash capture are read-only, all remediation occurs in a temporary copy, and a missing/unverifiable source path must fail the gate rather than silently substituting a synthetic fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The gate identifies the real local source path and records its pre/post content inventory and git state without writing, staging, committing, or changing its active scope selection.

The temporary copy preserves the observed string-origin legacy debt and historical variants before remediation, applies the candidate package using explicit canonical values, and reaches Doctor exit 0 plus a valid recertification without historical hash drift.

Lens reads only the temporary result and independently derives the expected remediated or recertified provenance, including the exact canonical after-image and retired legacy keys; no Lens test or app path writes the scope.
Failure to locate the original scope, a mismatch with the faithful shape, any original-tree byte drift, or a non-healthy Lens result fails the aggregate gate with an actionable reason.

evidence.summary: The real incident is now proven against BOTH runtimes: source dist and the candidate tarball installed into a fresh temporary prefix, each in its own independent temporary copy of the original scope, each verified separately by Lens. probeOriginalScope() takes the runtime as a parameter instead of hardcoding dist/cli.js. Gate at 469 assertions (was 407). The original Aliva checkout remains byte-identical, git-clean and un-rescoped.
validation: REVIEW FIX. probeOriginalScope(projectRoot, runtime) is now parameterized; the previous version hardcoded distRoot/cli.js, so the gate proved only that the source checkout could repair model-catalog-and-routing, never that kyro-ai@4.44.0 as packaged could. That was the exact limit R8 exists to remove.

Both runtimes run the real scope end to end, each in its OWN fresh temp copy: canonicalize-prepare READY, remediate apply, exactly seven canonical keys, archive checkpoint/snapshot/narrative SHA-256 and ledger commitments unchanged, doctor --artifacts exit 0, recertify apply, status 'Verification: recertified'. Gate output: 'original copy / source dist: repaired at protocol v3, doctor clean, recertified' and 'original copy / installed candidate package: repaired at protocol v3, doctor clean, recertified'.

Lens verifies EACH runtime's result separately, including the packaged one: 'Lens verified 2 tests on v22.22.1 (read-only)' reported for both copies. The gate asserts !requireLens || viaPackage.lens.run, so the packaged result cannot pass unverified, and it still requires exactly 2 PASSED so a skipped suite fails rather than reporting a vacuous green.

Cross-runtime agreement is asserted between two independently produced artifacts: identical canonical after-image, identical retiredKeys, and the two remediation RECORDS identical once createdAt is set aside. Both records are re-read from disk per runtime rather than compared to a shared expectation.

An over-strong assertion was found and corrected rather than worked around. Requiring chainHead equality across runtimes failed (source d30ae85c... vs package 95fe82b8...). A remediation record carries createdAt, so two runs minutes apart must hash differently by design; comparing the records modulo the timestamp is both correct and stronger. The gate now also asserts the converse - that differing timestamps cannot share a commitment - so the head is proven to bind createdAt.

The installed candidate is kept alive for this probe: installCandidatePackage() returns the runtime and registers temp-prefix cleanup on process exit, so the packaged CLI is available to the real-scope probe instead of being torn down after the fixture flow.

Original untouched, verified after BOTH probes: git status --porcelain empty, HEAD 34fdc055a56c07458d50f129be0e27c6aebded5f, D1 still carries origin 'food-analysis FR-FA-013 revision' and all three legacy keys, remediations still 0. The gate independently compares the scope's SHA-256 inventory, git state and local.json before and after each run.
Full gate: node scripts/check-original-incident-release.mjs --original-scope <aliva> --require-original-scope --lens <kyro-lens> --lens-node <node22> --require-lens => 469 assertions passed.
Lens on Node v22.22.1: tsc -b --force exit 0; full suite 64 files, 879 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
evidence.notes: Earlier defects in this task's tests, all mine and all caught by the tools rather than assumed away: Lens key-order (its parser rebuilds each debt, so order belongs to the raw bytes, where Kyro had written the exact canonical order); DIVERGED on unreadable certification evidence (addressed workspace-relative, my loader exposed only the scope dir); three TS2339 errors hidden by a vacuous typecheck. debt.title: Lens assistant-model-select suite fails on localStorage.clear in the current vitest/jsdom environment
debt.note: Misdiagnosed as a Lens defect. Reproduced only on Node v25.2.1, whose native localStorage (--localstorage-file) shadows the jsdom global and breaks localStorage.clear. On Node v22.22.1, within the engines range >=20, the pre-change baseline is 844 passed / 0 failed and assistant-model-select and sprint-board are green. No Lens change is warranted.

debt.title: Lens assistant chat-draft store leaks across test files, so an added test file changes assistant-chat.test.tsx's result
debt.note: Resolved in Sprint 5 / T5.1, and the original diagnosis was wrong. Not a cross-file leak and not a draft-store defect: assistant-chat.test.tsx advanced past an in-flight send as soon as the streamed reply rendered, while sending was still true. AssistantSessionList renders session buttons disabled={busy} (busy = sending || sessionBusy), so click() on a disabled button was a silent no-op, the chat never switched, and the assertion read the sending chat's empty draft. Isolation disproved the cross-file framing: the file alone failed 1 of 3 runs; the single test alone passed 5 of 5. Fixed in test synchronization only, via a clickWhenEnabled() helper that waits for the control to be enabled and fails loudly otherwise; no production change, no retries, no test-order pinning, no suite serialization, no global-state clearing. Regression 'blocks chat switching until a turn settles, without touching parked drafts' holds a turn open with a gated stream, asserts selection is disabled in that window and that a click there is a no-op, then asserts the parked draft survives; mutating disabled={busy} to disabled={false} makes it fail (source restored). Node v22.22.1: five consecutive full runs at 64 files / 879 tests, 0 failed; tsc --noEmit exit 0; vite build ok; guard mutations 16 assertions over 4 guards.

intendedAfterClose.title: Canonical Debt Contract and Legacy Remediation
intendedAfterClose.objective: Reconcile Kyro and Lens debt input semantics and deliver a typed append-only canonicalization path that repairs and recertifies closed legacy scopes without changing immutable history.
successCriteria: Kyro and Lens classify every canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported debt fixture identically.
An operator can prepare, preview, and atomically canonicalize the motivating legacy debt without manually calculating digests or editing managed files.
A successful repair changes only the targeted live debt and appended provenance while every historical artifact and commitment remains byte-identical.
Doctor, status, recertification, and Lens independently agree that a valid corrected scope is remediated or recertified and reject every forged, stale, partial, or unsupported variant.
The faithful original-incident scenario passes through the isolated package and projected runtime before publication.

requirements.statement: Kyro and Lens must distinguish canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported raw debts using the same observable contract.
requirements.rationale: Raw compatibility and canonical output are different responsibilities. Shared golden vectors, including the original D1 variants, must prove identical classification and canonical projection so the output interface is never again mistaken for the input schema.

requirements.statement: All new debt writes and successful remediations must emit exactly the seven-field canonical debt representation.
requirements.rationale: The canonical key set is id, title, origin, priority, status, targetSprint, and note. Exact output prevents hybrid legacy shapes while compatibility readers remain able to diagnose old input.

requirements.statement: A new versioned debt canonicalization operation must bind the complete observed debt and produce an explicit exact canonical after-image.
requirements.rationale: The existing origin-only operation cannot repair the motivating scope. A closed debt.canonicalize operation must preserve identity fields, require explicit canonical values, retire legacy-only keys, use a whole-debt SHA-256 precondition, and resolve multiple field issues atomically without becoming a generic patch.

requirements.statement: Preparation and preview must be read-only, derive all technical digests, expose evidence and unresolved decisions, and never treat suggested values as operator authorization.
requirements.rationale: Origin has strong addedSprint evidence, while priority and target sprint remain business judgments. INPUT_REQUIRED must name every unresolved value, and a complete manifest must be producible without hand-editing managed state or manually calculating hashes.

requirements.statement: Canonicalization apply and resume must remain atomic, append-only, idempotent, and history-preserving under the state-writer lock.
requirements.rationale: Checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, ledger commitment, task, verdict, unrelated debt, and existing provenance bytes are immutable. Stale full-debt state, interruption, or post-write mismatch must produce no competing applied record and must preserve deterministic PREPARED resume.

requirements.statement: Doctor, status, replay, and recertification must support existing and new remediation versions without weakening historical integrity or tamper detection.
requirements.rationale: The new operation requires an explicit protocol revision so old readers fail closed as unsupported. New readers must replay v1, v2, new, and mixed chains; historical schema notes must never short-circuit artifact digest checks; C-NNN must bind the current head.

requirements.statement: Lens must independently verify and render legacy classification, canonicalization provenance, remediation state, and recertification state.
requirements.rationale: Lens is a read-only verifier, not a consumer of Kyro's claimed label. It must recompute commitments and result state, render selected values and retired legacy keys, and show actionable diagnostics with no stale-state fallback.

requirements.statement: A faithful original-incident fixture and a temporary-copy probe of the actual local scope must gate the packaged and installed release.
requirements.rationale: Synthetic canonical fixtures missed the contradiction. Sentinel assertions must preserve the string origin and missing-field shapes; the full before, prepare, preview, apply, Doctor, recertify, and Lens flow must pass with unchanged historical hashes through an isolated package and projected runtime.

requirements.statement: Release documentation must state the Kyro 4.43.5 limitation, compatible upgrade order, operator workflow, and exact certification boundary.
requirements.rationale: Users must not be told that origin-only remediation repairs record-level legacy drift. Documentation must separate local/source success from package, installed-runtime, Lens, and publication evidence.

scenarios.when: They follow the published upgrade, explicit-value, remediation, recertification, and Lens verification instructions
scenarios.then: The documentation and its executable checker distinguish every evidence boundary, forbid silent inference and historical rewriting, and do not claim global installation or publication from local candidate evidence

nonGoals: Rewrite or replace historical checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, or ledger evidence.
Introduce generic JSON Patch or arbitrary path mutation.
Infer priority, target sprint, origin, or note semantics without explicit operator authorization.
Recover missing or corrupted checkpoint bytes from backup or Git.
Canonicalize tasks, verdicts, ADRs, conventions, or non-debt SprintFile structures.
Mutate every legacy scope automatically during installation or Doctor.
Retain legacy-only debt keys in the corrected live canonical object.
Break or rewrite existing v1 or v2 remediation and certification records.
Modify, stage, or commit files in the original Aliva checkout during release validation.
Claim production readiness beyond the covered debt compatibility and append-only remediation contract.

conventions.rule: Never rewrite committed checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, or ledger commitments; remediation may only append provenance and replace the live canonical projection.
Treat inferred legacy values as suggestions only; apply requires explicit operator-supplied canonical values in the manifest.
Every raw-debt classification or canonical projection change must update and pass the shared Kyro and Lens golden vectors.
Do not claim the incident fixed until the faithful legacy fixture passes source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens gates.
Probe the actual Aliva scope only through read-only inspection and a temporary copy; never mutate, stage, or commit its checkout during Kyro release validation.

adrs.title: Separate raw debt compatibility from canonical debt output
adrs.context: The incident recurred because Kyro treated the strict Debt output interface as the raw input contract while Lens intentionally normalizes legacy input.
adrs.decision: Classify raw debt as canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, or unsupported, and preserve an exact seven-field canonical output contract for all new writes.
consequences: Doctor and Lens can understand legacy data without calling it canonical, and writers remain strict.
Shared behavior vectors become a compatibility contract across repositories.
alternatives: Use one strict schema for both input and output.
Allow Lens-only defaults without a Kyro classification.

adrs.title: Canonicalize legacy debt as one typed record-level operation
adrs.context: The existing debt.origin.set operation cannot add missing canonical fields or retire legacy-only keys, so strict post-state validation makes the motivating scope unrecoverable.
adrs.decision: Introduce a closed debt.canonicalize operation with a whole-debt digest precondition, preserved identity fields, explicit canonical values, and an exact seven-key after-image.
consequences: One atomic R-NNN resolves all related field issues without intermediate hybrid states.
Routine isolated edits remain owned by normal debt commands rather than remediation.
alternatives: Add independent setters for every debt field.
Expose generic JSON Patch or JSON Pointer mutations.

adrs.title: Version the canonicalization operation as a new protocol revision
adrs.context: Existing Kyro and Lens readers know only the current remediation versions and debt.origin.set semantics.
adrs.decision: Publish debt.canonicalize in a new explicit remediation protocol revision with version-aware replay and mixed-chain coverage.
consequences: Older readers fail closed as unsupported instead of interpreting a known version differently.
New readers must preserve byte-compatible verification of every existing v1 and v2 chain.
alternatives: Add the new operation silently to an existing schema version.
Drop replay support for older remediation records.

adrs.title: Require explicit semantic authority and retire live legacy keys
adrs.context: AddedSprint supports an origin suggestion, but priority and target sprint are business decisions; retaining detail, resolution, or addedSprint would leave a hybrid live contract.
adrs.decision: Preparation may suggest values with evidence, but apply requires explicit operator values and emits exactly the seven canonical debt keys while preserving old bytes only through immutable history and remediation provenance.
consequences: The record distinguishes observed evidence from operator judgment.
Legacy-only keys disappear from live state without erasing historical proof.
alternatives: Silently adopt Lens defaults as historical truth.
Keep legacy-only keys alongside canonical fields.

adrs.title: Gate release on the motivating artifact shape
adrs.context: Synthetic fixtures with otherwise canonical debt allowed the previous implementation to pass while the real model-catalog-and-routing scope remained impossible to remediate.
adrs.decision: Require a faithful minimized fixture plus a temporary-copy probe of the actual scope through source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens before publication.
consequences: Fixture sentinel assertions prevent future cleanup from deleting the failure shape.
The original Aliva checkout remains read-only throughout certification.
alternatives: Certify only generated canonical fixtures.
Apply the candidate directly to the original project checkout.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Five sprints follow the dependency chain and isolate independent failure domains. Sprint 1 freezes the raw/canonical contract and faithful reproduction before writers depend on it. Sprint 2 adds the versioned typed operation and operator preparation under the existing transaction model. Sprint 3 proves replay, Doctor, status, and recertification integrity across old, new, and mixed chains. Sprint 4 updates Lens as an independent cross-repository verifier only after Kyro's protocol stabilizes. Sprint 5 certifies the faithful original incident through packaging, projected runtime, Lens, and documentation. Fewer sprints would let writer, verifier, consumer, or release evidence falsely certify one another; more would split cohesive gates without reducing risk. The plan's acceptance matrix is allocated to the relevant sprint as Given/When/Then scenarios during per-sprint planning.

sprints.title: Debt contract reconciliation and faithful fixtures

recommendations: Keep Sprint 2 limited to the typed operation schema and read-only preparation; do not introduce apply or mutate immutable history before the transaction and replay gates in Sprint 3.
Sprint 3 must implement atomic apply, resume, replay, and recertification under the state-writer lock without weakening historical integrity.
Lens contract parity in Sprint 4 requires independent verification of the new canonicalization provenance and remediation state.
Sprint 4 must independently verify v3 canonicalization provenance, unanchored or PREPARED records, and chain-head-bound recertification in Lens.
Keep Lens read-only and mirror Kyro fail-closed chain semantics without trusting Kyro status labels.
Sprint 5 must resolve the deferred Lens assistant draft-store isolation failure under a pinned supported Node runtime before claiming a green release suite.
Sprint 5 must run the faithful original incident only in a temporary copy through source, isolated package, installed or projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens without touching Aliva.
Sprint 5 must publish R9 operator documentation with the 4.43.5 origin-only limitation, upgrade order, and exact evidence boundary.
Before npm publication, commit the certified 4.44.0 changes, run hosted CI, and publish only after its separate release gate passes.
After publication, update the installed Kyro runtime deliberately; do not treat the current 4.43.5 global runtime as the 4.44.0 candidate.

debt.title: Lens assistant-model-select suite fails on localStorage.clear in the current vitest/jsdom environment
debt.note: Misdiagnosed as a Lens defect. Reproduced only on Node v25.2.1, whose native localStorage (--localstorage-file) shadows the jsdom global and breaks localStorage.clear. On Node v22.22.1, within the engines range >=20, the pre-change baseline is 844 passed / 0 failed and assistant-model-select and sprint-board are green. No Lens change is warranted.

debt.title: Lens assistant chat-draft store leaks across test files, so an added test file changes assistant-chat.test.tsx's result
debt.note: Resolved in Sprint 5 / T5.1, and the original diagnosis was wrong. Not a cross-file leak and not a draft-store defect: assistant-chat.test.tsx advanced past an in-flight send as soon as the streamed reply rendered, while sending was still true. AssistantSessionList renders session buttons disabled={busy} (busy = sending || sessionBusy), so click() on a disabled button was a silent no-op, the chat never switched, and the assertion read the sending chat's empty draft. Isolation disproved the cross-file framing: the file alone failed 1 of 3 runs; the single test alone passed 5 of 5. Fixed in test synchronization only, via a clickWhenEnabled() helper that waits for the control to be enabled and fails loudly otherwise; no production change, no retries, no test-order pinning, no suite serialization, no global-state clearing. Regression 'blocks chat switching until a turn settles, without touching parked drafts' holds a turn open with a gated stream, asserts selection is disabled in that window and that a click there is a no-op, then asserts the parked draft survives; mutating disabled={busy} to disabled={false} makes it fail (source restored). Node v22.22.1: five consecutive full runs at 64 files / 879 tests, 0 failed; tsc --noEmit exit 0; vite build ok; guard mutations 16 assertions over 4 guards.

handoff.note: Sprint 5 (original-incident-release-gate) closed as shipped. No sprints remain — scope objective met.
